rounds.text: The market is pricing Kedia Construction Company Ltd at an astonishingly low price-to-book ratio of 0.05x, trading at just ₹ 2.45 against a book value of ₹ 49.5 [E1], despite the entire enterprise commanding a micro-capitalisation of only ₹ 0.73 Cr [E2]. This extreme asset discount completely ignores a strong, long-term top-line expansion, evidenced by compounded sales growth of 19% over 10 years and accelerating to 21% over 5 years [E6, E7]. Crucially, recent operational performance shows massive inflection potential, demonstrated by a staggering trailing twelve-month sales growth of 83% [E9] and a dramatic quarterly operating margin surge to 825% in March 2026, marking a 967 percentage point improvement over the year-ago quarter [E16]. These powerful operational recoveries triggered positive screening signals for year-over-year profit growth exceeding 20% and accelerating earnings [E40, E42]. Conceded: [E3], [E4], [E5], [E10], [E15], [E43].

The apparent discount of a 0.05x price-to-book ratio is completely illusory when evaluated against the company's severe capital destruction and operating collapse [E1, E4, E5]. Both return on capital employed and return on equity stand deeply negative at -24.8% and -25.2% respectively, proving that the underlying asset base is actively losing value rather than compounding for shareholders [E4, E5]. Furthermore, compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has cratered by -23400%, accompanied by an annual operating margin that plunged to -471% against a positive margin three years prior [E10, E15]. This catastrophic margin compression of 631 percentage points highlights a total lack of operational stability, reinforced by a severe annual sales contraction of 67% year-on-year flagged by the screening engine [E15, E43]. To compound these fundamental weaknesses, the stock offers a zero dividend yield, leaving investors with neither current income nor profitable growth to justify the asset's ownership [E3]. Conceded: [E6].

The bear condemns the asset base, but the extreme price-to-book ratio of 0.05x—trading at ₹ 2.45 against a book value of ₹ 49.5—more than adequately prices in past negative returns, leaving the downside heavily cushioned [E1, E4, E5]. While the annual operating margin suffered a deep contraction, the most recent evidence reveals a dramatic turnaround with a quarterly operating margin of 825% in Mar 2026, representing a massive 967 percentage point expansion over the year-ago quarter [E15, E16]. This operational inflection directly powers the screening engine signals for year-on-year profit growth exceeding 20% and accelerating earnings growth [E40, E42]. Furthermore, the company's long-term top-line expansion remains robust with 10-year compounded sales growth at 19% and 5-year growth at 21%, reinforced by a sharp acceleration in trailing twelve-month sales growth to 83% [E6, E7, E9]. Conceded: [E3, E10, E43].

The bull relies on the 0.05x price-to-book ratio as a margin of safety, but a low multiple offers no protection when fundamental wealth destruction is ongoing, as evidenced by an ROE of -25.2% and an ROCE of -24.8% [E1, E4, E5]. While the bull cites a single quarter's operating margin of 825% in Mar 2026, this extreme volatility exists alongside a collapsing annual operating margin of -471% and a catastrophic compounded trailing twelve-month profit growth of -23400% [E10, E15, E16]. The bull points to long-term top-line expansion and an 83% TTM sales growth rate, but these metrics are directly contradicted by concurrent screening evidence showing a severe sales contraction of -67% year-on-year [E6, E7, E9, E43]. Conceded: [E16, E40, E42].
